To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
reverse transcriptase is present in human leukaemic cells and is associated with a high-molecular-weight virus-related RNA.

human leukaemic cells are infected with a virus which is closely related to the Rauscher murine leukaemia virus, and that the virus is present in the cells as a high molecular weight RNA complexed to reverse transcriptase.

the DNA synthesized by the complexes of RNA and reverse transcriptate isolated from leukaemic cells hybridizes to the Rauscher RNA and does not hybridize to either the myeloblasts virus RNA or the mammary tumour RNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of reverse transcriptase associated complexes from human leukaemic cells.
the identification of the virus associated with human leukaemia and its role in the development of this disease.
the isolation of the RNA of the human leukaemia virus from human leukaemic cells and with the synthesis of the DNA complementary to this RNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reverse transcriptase found in human leukaemic cells appears to be associated with a virus-related RNA that is closely related to that found in the Rauscher strain of murine leukaemia virus.

the reverse transcriptase associated RNA of the leukaemic cells has been shown to be a high molecular weight RNA and that it is related to the RNA of Rauscher leukeamia virus, but is not related to the RNA's of the avian myelo-blastosis virus or the mouse mammary tumor virus.
a virus-related RNA is present in the leukaemic cells and that this RNA can be transcribed to DNA by an enzyme, reverse transcriptase, which is present in the cell.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human leukaemic cells examined contain a virus-related RNA which is transcribed by a reverse transcriptase into a double-stranded DNA.
we have found that human leukaemic cells are infected by a virus related to the Rauscher virus.
the human leukaemias are associated with a high incidence of a retrovirus, which we have named human type C virus (HTC).
The main takeaway from our work is that

we now have a way to detect the presence of the retroviral DNA in the blood cells of leukaemic people, and that we now know that the retroviral RNA is present as a complex with the reverse transcriptase.
reverse transcriptase is associated with a high-molecular-weight RNA in human leukemic cells and that complexes of reverse transcriptase and RNA can be isolated from human leukemic cells.
reverse transcriptase is a common component of human leukaemic cells and that it is associated with virus-like RNA.
